description: A three-panel TEM study of the uniformly deformed gauge region after tensile testing. (a) Bright-field TEM micrograph of M1-30 with a 200 nm scale bar (bottom-left); heavy dark dislocation tangles and cell walls fill the whole field, and a band running diagonally across the image is annotated "Slip band" in yellow with a yellow dotted line. (b) TEM micrograph of M2-30 at the same 200 nm scale bar; the matrix shows finer, mottled high-density contrast, a yellow dotted "Slip band" annotation marks a narrower banded region, and a blue dashed square with blue dashed leaders encloses a small area to be magnified. (c) Higher-magnification TEM image of that boxed area with a 30 nm scale bar, in which a blue line and the blue label "(Ti, V) Carbides" point to an individual dark nanoscale carbide particle embedded in the fine precipitate/dislocation structure. Taken together the panels argue that both M1-30 and M2-30 deform by planar dislocation slip (a, b), that the slip bands are finer in M2-30, and that non-shearable (Ti, V)C carbides obstruct dislocations (c). No numeric slip-band spacings are printed on any panel.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a TEM micrograph of M1-30 with a 200 nm scale bar and a yellow dotted annotation reading "Slip band" placed along a diagonal band.
Panel (b) is a TEM micrograph of M2-30 with a 200 nm scale bar, a yellow dotted "Slip band" annotation, and a blue dashed square whose dashed leaders indicate the region enlarged in panel (c).
Panel (c) has a 30 nm scale bar and a blue label "(Ti, V) Carbides" with a blue line pointing to a single dark nanoscale particle, roughly an order of magnitude smaller than the 30 nm scale bar.

Panel (a) is dominated by long, curved, dark dislocation lines forming tangles and cell walls, whereas panel (b) shows finer, more densely speckled contrast with narrower bands, consistent with a smaller slip-band spacing in M2-30.
No numeric slip-band spacing or dislocation-density values are printed on any panel; the only printed quantities are the scale bars 200 nm (a, b) and 30 nm (c).
The caption states the figure shows TEM images of M1-30 (a) and M2-30 (b, c) after tensile deformation.
The citing text states that the uniformly deformed region in Fig. 12(a) and (b) shows the deformation mode of both M1 and M2 to be plane slip of dislocations, consistent with the SFE calculation.
The citing text states that the slip-band spacing of M2 steel is significantly smaller than that of M1 steel, indicating more severe deformation of M2 (a numeric value is not given).
The citing text states that homogeneous κ-carbide precipitation prevents refinement of the slip band and lowers the work-hardening index of M1 after aging.
The citing text states that (Ti, V)C carbides hinder dislocations, as shown in Fig. 12(c), and that a region of higher dislocation density forms around them, increasing the flow stress.
The citing text states that the size of κ-carbides in M2 decreases slightly and their volume fraction decreases relative to M1.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph of M1-30 after tensile deformation, 200 nm scale bar at bottom-left. Dense dark dislocation tangles/cells cover the field; a diagonal band is marked "Slip band" in yellow with a yellow dotted line.

TEM micrograph of M2-30 after tensile deformation, 200 nm scale bar at bottom-left. Finer, more mottled dark contrast; a yellow dotted line labelled "Slip band"; a blue dashed square with blue dashed leaders marks the region shown at higher magnification in (c).

Higher-magnification TEM image of the region boxed in (b), 30 nm scale bar at bottom-left. A blue line from the blue label "(Ti, V) Carbides" points to a dark nanoscale particle within a fine, speckled precipitate/dislocation microstructure.
